The ceremony's own script names the match "the World Title Cage Match at Fear the Raine"; the following year's ceremony instead calls the same pairing's win a match "at March Maelstrom II" — the two GIWF ceremony scripts disagree with each other on the event name, not just with any outside source; recorded as an open discrepancy between two primary documents rather than silently resolved. CORRECTED from an earlier registry entry that credited the-phenomenons here, sourced only from a later, self-attested Hall of Fame induction boast. The actual GIWF ceremony transcript — a live, contemporary primary source — settles it: the Phenomenons placed in that three-way tie for third at 23%, not first. See giwf-2000-match-of-the-year's own provenance note for where the Phenomenons' real Match of the Year win actually landed.

47.06%, Venetian Home Rumble I — the Phenomenons vs. Al Crud & the joke gimmick Tom the Christmas Tree, fought at Christmas Clash '99 — over Slasher/CA$H's THC Title War (23.53%), the Nightmare Reflections Match (17.65%), and Al Crud/Pete Steele's Regal Rumble main event (11.76%). PROVENANCE NOTE, resolving a dating discrepancy: a Phenomenons Hall of Fame induction speech elsewhere self-attests a "1999 GIWF Match of the Year" win for this same Venetian Home Rumble; the actual match happened at a Dec 1999 show, but the GIWF's own annual-awards cycle crowned it at the ceremony covering "year 2000" (the 1999 ceremony's own Match of the Year, held only weeks earlier, had already gone to Curt Raines & Hamish McGrubber — see giwf-1999-match-of-the-year). Read together, the two contemporary ceremony transcripts show the HOF speech's own claim as misdated by one ceremony cycle, not fabricated: right match, wrong year named. Both rows stand, each receipted to its own ceremony's own primary transcript. Independently corroborated by a later UWF retrospective ("the battle... that had won the 2000 Match of the Year award") and a Christmas Clash 2000 preview calling Rumble I the favorite for the award.

name: Universal Tag Team Titles (self-awarded)
epitaph: A foam belt, never a sanctioned GIWF championship, that the Phenomenons gave themselves and wore in-character as though it outranked their six real title reigns — three times World Tag Team Champions, three times North American — yet left off the Accomplishments in their own GIWF bio. When Deke Aurora and Nephilim snatched the belts at ringside on 29 August 1999, a new pair from the GIWF catalogue arrived three days later; no one else ever claimed the title: it was always just theirs.
notes: Source: the Phenomenons' own GIWF bio page, which describes each man as “always” wearing his “Universal Tag Team Title belt”; and the GIWF's own cards, where the belts appear from Suicide of 29 August 1999 to Global of 1 August 2001.

bestowals.vote_detail: Given by the Phenomenons to themselves: GIWF merchandise foam belts trimmed in gold, which the two of them wore to the ring as the Universal Tag Team Titles and billed above their real championships. On the fed's own cards from 29 August 1999 to 1 August 2001; no date of the self-awarding itself survives.
bestowals.source: The GIWF's own cards, among them Suicide of 29 August 1999 (promotions/giwf/archive/suicide-1999-08-29.html: "They carry round Foam belts with gold trim and you recognise those as genuine universal tag-team straps?????"), Quake of 30 September 1999 (promotions/giwf/archive/quake.html: "GIWF Merchandising foam belts decorated with gold leaf and declare themselves to be the Universal Tag Team champions"), Global of 6 July 2000 (promotions/giwf/archive/global-2000-07-06.html: "the current GIWF Universal Tag Team Champions") and Global of 1 August 2001 (promotions/giwf/archive/global-2001-08-01.html); and the Phenomenons' own GIWF bio page, which describes each man as "always" wearing his "Universal Tag Team Title belt".
